results.title: 5 Essential Steam Deck Apps You Should Be Using In 2026
results.content:
Now that you have a launcher set up to easily launch all of your games, you're going to want to install Decky Loader to gain access to a wide world of Steam Deck plugins. Accessible from a single button press, Decky Loader is basically a Swiss Army Knife for the Steam Deck. Plugins range from customizing with new visuals and sounds, to tweaking your games' performance on a per-game basis, even including games you emulate with apps like EmuDeck (more on that later). [...] By using ProtonUp-Qt, you can ensure you have Proton-GE installed for your Steam Deck games to access, and you can even choose what versions, should you need an older variant to get a game working. Once you've installed your Proton-GE version of choice, you'll be able to select that Proton version just as you would with the defaults already available on Steam.

ProtonUp-Qt is one of the easiest ways to extend game compatibility on the Steam Deck, and since it's available on the Linux app store Flathub as a Flatpak, it's also easy to install. Steam OS supports Flatpaks from Flathub out of the box within the default Discover Software Center. Simply boot into the Desktop Mode, open Discover, and search for ProtonUp-Qt to install it. Easy-peasy, just as handheld gaming was meant to be. [...] ## ProtonUp-Qt

One of the great things about Steam OS and the Steam Deck is that you can easily change your Proton versions on a per-game basis. You may want to do this to find a Proton version that performs better in a game than the default option. The thing is, despite how many versions of Proton are out there, you are limited to a handful on the default Steam Deck setup. This is where ProtonUp-Qt comes into the picture: This tool makes it easy to install Proton-GE, a community-made fork that offers extra patches for extended compatibility, thanks to its friendly graphical user interface.

, communication tools (Slack), and entertainment apps (Spotify).
   Flutter: Emerging as a choice for media-rich applications, Flutter has been used for apps like Google Ads, Alibaba, and Reflectly.
   Tauri: Tauri is gaining traction for lightweight, secure applications, including password managers (LosePass) and communication tools (Mailspring).
   React Native: Although primarily a mobile framework, React Native has been extended for desktop use in apps like Discord and Microsoft Teams.
   Qt: Qt is a versatile choice used in a wide range of applications, from industrial software to gaming and automotive infotainment systems.

## Development Challenges [...] If you’re looking for a framework that allows you to leverage web technologies, Electron and React Native are strong choices. Electron has a large community and a wide range of pre-built components, while React Native offers a robust component system and allows for code reuse between mobile and desktop platforms.
   If performance and small bundle sizes are a priority, consider Flutter or Tauri. Flutter provides fast startup times and smooth animations, while Tauri is known for its lightweight nature and low resource consumption.
   If you need a framework with excellent native integration and a native look and feel, Qt is a reliable option. [...] ## Development Challenges

While each framework has its strengths, it’s essential to be aware of potential challenges and limitations:

   Electron: Electron apps can be resource-intensive, potentially leading to performance issues on older hardware.
   Flutter: Developing for desktop with Flutter may involve a learning curve if you’re primarily a mobile developer.
   Tauri: As a relatively new framework, Tauri may have a smaller community and fewer third-party libraries compared to more established options.
   React Native: Transitioning React Native to desktop may require additional effort, and some platform-specific features may be harder to access
   Qt: Qt’s learning curve, particularly for developers new to C++, may be a challenge.

## Conclusion
